experiment_description: Central concept: use thin, crystalline, optically transparent muscovite mica as a polymer-free van der Waals transfer medium whose adhesion to 2D materials is tuned by temperature, enabling deterministic pick-up, stacking, and release without organic polymer contact. Atomic-force-microscopy-grade muscovite crystals are mechanically exfoliated with adhesive tape to produce few-hundred-nanometer-thick mica layers. For membrane stamps, a mica sheet is suspended over a 5–6 mm punched hole in Nitto ELP BT-50E-FR tape or several layers of Scotch Magic tape, transferred onto a rectangular PDMS block on a microscope glass slide, and tensioned by fixing the tape to the glass-slide sides. For cantilever stamps, a triangular mica sheet is cleaved from the tape edge, mounted on a metal support angled about 15 degrees on a microscope glass slide, and used as a freestanding transparent cantilever. Source mica and prepared stamps are stored under inert gas or in a dry vacuum desiccator; transfers are performed in argon glove-box or air conditions with ambient relative humidity kept below about 50% to limit water adsorption. For hBN/graphene/hBN assembly, a Si/SiO2 substrate containing an hBN flake is preheated to 50–90 °C, the mica stamp is brought into contact under an optical microscope by z-axis motion, the contact front is moved by z approach or by changing substrate temperature within ±10 °C, and full contact is made with the target flake before retraction. Subsequent 2D layers such as graphene are picked up using the already collected top hBN. For release, a target substrate carrying a bottom hBN flake is heated to 120–180 °C; the stack is brought into contact with the bottom hBN and the contact front is swept by temperature variation while leaving part of the bottom hBN uncovered by mica to test selective release of only the intended stack. The spatial scope is optical-microscope-guided flake-scale transfer over tens of micrometers in the active heterostructure region, using the mica membrane or cantilever as the only solid transfer support in place of PC/PPC polymer.

polymer_free_hbn_graphene_hbn_heterostru.description: Whether the mica membrane or cantilever protocol produced the intended hBN/graphene/hBN van der Waals heterostructure without a polymer transfer layer contacting the stack.

selective_stack_release_onto_bottom_hbn_.description: Whether the temperature-controlled mica protocol enabled release of the intended stack onto bottom hBN while retaining unwanted picked-up flakes on the mica stamp.

experiment_description: Central concept: evaluate whether the polymer-free mica cantilever transfer leaves atomically flat, clean hBN-encapsulated graphene interfaces without solvent cleaning or annealing. A single-layer graphene flake is fully encapsulated between top and bottom hBN using mica-cantilever-assisted assembly and the standard bottom-hBN release mechanism. The released stack is characterized as-is by contact-mode atomic force microscopy over the working area of the heterostructure, with the roughness extracted from a defined interior analysis window inside a several-micrometer AFM scan, away from visible flake edges and macroscopic contamination pockets. The measurement targets surface height variations of the top hBN over the active graphene-containing region after polymer-free release.

surface_rms_roughness_pm.description: The root-mean-square topographic roughness of the mica-cantilever-assembled hBN-encapsulated single-layer graphene stack measured in the selected AFM analysis window.

surface_peak_to_peak_roughness_pm.description: The peak-to-peak topographic roughness of the mica-cantilever-assembled hBN-encapsulated single-layer graphene stack measured in the selected AFM analysis window.

experiment_description: Central concept: test a polymer-free bottom-up assembly route in which a mica cantilever is incorporated as the supporting substrate by flipping the assembly and mechanically breaking off the cantilever, avoiding reliance on an additional bottom hBN release flake. A single-layer graphene flake is encapsulated in hBN on a graphite gate electrode using a mica cantilever; the cantilever is then flipped, broken off, and retained below the heterostructure as a mica layer. The sample is examined as-is by contact-mode AFM on the active hBN/graphene/hBN/graphite region, with roughness calculated from an interior analysis box inside a several-micrometer scan, away from flake boundaries and visible defects. The measurement targets whether the mica-supported heterostructure has an atomically flat exposed top surface after the polymer-free break-off release.

surface_rms_roughness_pm.description: The root-mean-square topographic roughness of the mica-supported hBN-encapsulated single-layer graphene stack measured in the selected AFM analysis window.

surface_peak_to_peak_roughness_pm.description: The peak-to-peak topographic roughness of the mica-supported hBN-encapsulated single-layer graphene stack measured in the selected AFM analysis window.

experiment_description: Central concept: determine whether the mica membrane method can assemble a more complex multilayer van der Waals stack with clean interfaces and without post-transfer cleaning. A seven-layer heterostructure is assembled by mica-membrane-assisted transfer with the layer sequence hBN / twisted trilayer graphene / hBN / graphite / hBN; each graphene layer in the twisted trilayer graphene is intentionally misaligned by a high angle of about 20 degrees to decouple the graphene layers. The stack is released and characterized as-is without annealing, solvent immersion, or other cleaning. Contact-mode AFM is performed on the active multilayer region over an area exceeding 100 µm², and topographic roughness is extracted from an interior analysis window away from visible edges and bubbles. The measurement targets the surface flatness of the exposed top hBN above the multilayer graphene/graphite structure.

surface_rms_roughness_pm.description: The root-mean-square topographic roughness of the mica-membrane-assembled hBN/twisted-trilayer-graphene/hBN/graphite/hBN stack measured in the selected AFM analysis window.

surface_peak_to_peak_roughness_pm.description: The peak-to-peak topographic roughness of the mica-membrane-assembled hBN/twisted-trilayer-graphene/hBN/graphite/hBN stack measured in the selected AFM analysis window.

experiment_description: Central concept: assess whether mica-assisted assembly can produce a clean, marginally twisted hBN/hBN moiré ferroelectric superlattice over a large flake-scale area, using the atomically flat mica surface and low-temperature release to preserve the twist configuration. A cracked hBN flake is used so that one piece is picked up with a mica membrane and released back onto another part of the same hBN flake at 50 °C, targeting marginal angular alignment. The resulting hBN/hBN stack is characterized by AFM height imaging and Kelvin probe force microscopy under scanning-probe conditions. The KPFM scans target nanoscale electrostatic-potential modulation associated with triangular ferroelectric moiré domains over the top hBN flake, including a large-area scan of the whole flake-scale region and a higher-resolution scan near a localized submicron interfacial bubble to test continuity and local deformation of the domain pattern.

moire_ferroelectric_superlattice_formed.description: Whether the marginally twisted hBN/hBN structure produced by mica-assisted assembly exhibited a ferroelectric moiré superlattice detectable by KPFM.

moire_domain_coverage_area_um2.description: The approximate area of the top hBN flake over which the ferroelectric moiré domains extended in KPFM characterization.

hbn_moire_superlattice_fabrication_yield.description: The approximate fabrication yield for hBN-based moiré superlattice structures using the mica-assisted protocol, as reported for this structure class.

experiment_description: Central concept: compare the mica-assisted polymer-free route with a conventional polycarbonate-based assembly for marginally twisted hBN/hBN moiré ferroelectrics, focusing on whether surface residues obstruct scanning-probe detection of the interfacial moiré potential. A marginally twisted hBN/hBN structure is assembled using a standard PC-assisted method, most of the PC is dissolved in dichloromethane for several hours, and the exposed surface is examined by KPFM before and after local contact-mode AFM mechanical cleaning. The scan covers both polymer-residue-covered regions and an AFM-cleaned region on the hBN/hBN stack, using the same type of ferroelectric moiré electrostatic contrast targeted in the mica-assisted hBN/hBN measurement.

moire_potential_screened_by_pc_residues.description: Whether polymer residues on the PC-assembled hBN/hBN stack screened the KPFM-detectable moiré ferroelectric potential in residue-covered regions.

moire_potential_detectable_after_afm_cle.description: Whether local contact-mode AFM cleaning enabled KPFM detection of the hBN/hBN moiré ferroelectric potential in the cleaned region.

experiment_description: Central concept: test whether a pre-characterized marginally aligned single-layer graphene/hBN moiré heterostructure can be picked up by a mica membrane while preserving the moiré wavelength and therefore the twist angle. A single-layer graphene on hBN stack is first assembled on SiO2/Si by a PC-based method and characterized by peak-force microscopy in a clean area between PC-residue traces. The heterostructure is then picked up using a mica membrane at 50 °C and re-characterized with the same AFM cantilever while supported by mica. Peak-force microscopy line profiles are compared along defined line cuts in the pre-pickup and post-pickup scans over a nanoscale moiré region, targeting the periodic adhesion or indentation modulation of the SLG/hBN moiré lattice rather than macroscopic flake morphology.

moire_wavelength_on_sio2_nm.description: The SLG/hBN moiré wavelength measured by peak-force microscopy before mica pickup while the heterostructure was on SiO2/Si.

moire_wavelength_on_mica_nm.description: The SLG/hBN moiré wavelength measured by peak-force microscopy after pickup onto the mica membrane.

moire_twist_angle_preserved_after_mica_p.description: Whether comparison of the SLG/hBN moiré wavelength before and after mica pickup indicated preservation of the twist angle.

experiment_description: Central concept: use polymer-free mica-membrane assembly to expose clean conductive twisted bilayer graphene surfaces for high-resolution conductive AFM, while deterministically setting sub-degree twist angles to tune the moiré period. Marginal-angle twisted bilayer graphene devices are assembled on thick graphite flakes by the mica-membrane method with nominal twist angles of about 0.8°, 0.3°, and 0.15°. Conductive AFM is performed in ambient air at room temperature with relative humidity below 56% using a Bruker Dimension Icon AFM, Nanoscope VII controller, PFTUNA module, and Pt-coated Si CONTV-PT tip of approximate radius 25 nm and spring constant about 0.2 N/m. Scanning is in contact mode at 0.5–1 Hz. The 0.8° scan uses 1 mV sample bias, -0.1 V deflection setpoint, and 256 × 256 pixels; the 0.3° scans use 0.4 mV bias, 0.02 V setpoint, and 512 × 512 or 256 × 256 pixels; the 0.15° scans use 7 mV bias, 0.08 V or 0.05 V setpoint, and 512 × 512 or 256 × 256 pixels. Current maps are first-order flattened. The scans span nanoscale fields of view from tens to hundreds of nanometers and target local tip-sample current variation associated with AA/AB/BA domains and domain walls, with the broader uniformity context assessed across up to micrometer-scale exposed TBG surface.

moire_period_for_0p8deg_tbg_nm.description: The moiré period measured by conductive AFM for the approximately 0.8° twisted bilayer graphene device.

aa_ab_ba_domain_structure_resolved_in_lo.description: Whether conductive AFM resolved AA, AB, and BA domain contrast and associated domain-wall structure in the lower-angle twisted bilayer graphene devices.

uniform_moire_area_um2.description: The approximate maximum area over which the exposed twisted bilayer graphene moiré superlattice was reported to remain uniform and clean for cAFM/STM-scale studies.

experiment_description: Central concept: determine whether mica-assisted assembly yields graphene Hall-bar electronic quality comparable to state-of-the-art clean van der Waals devices. A large-area hBN/single-layer-graphene/hBN heterostructure is assembled on SiO2/Si using the mica-assisted method and patterned into a Hall bar in a bubble-free region with approximate dimensions 20 µm by 14 µm. Low-temperature multiterminal non-local bend-resistance measurements are performed at T = 1.7 K. Charge-carrier density n is swept over approximately -1.5 × 10^12 to +1.0 × 10^12 cm^-2 and perpendicular magnetic field B over approximately -0.3 to +0.3 T in the non-local geometry, with current and voltage probes arranged across the Hall-bar width. The measurement targets ballistic transport signatures, magnetic electron focusing, and mobility as functions of carrier density in the active encapsulated graphene channel.

zero_field_negative_nonlocal_resistance_.description: Whether the hBN-encapsulated single-layer graphene Hall bar exhibited negative non-local resistance at zero magnetic field in the bend-resistance geometry.

magnetic_electron_focusing_observed.description: Whether the non-local magnetotransport exhibited magnetic electron focusing oscillations.

high_density_electron_mobility_cm2_V_s.description: The electron mobility reached at high carrier density in the hBN-encapsulated single-layer graphene Hall bar.

experiment_description: Central concept: test the mica-assisted method on a complex, high-angle twisted trilayer graphene heterostructure where low disorder and ballisticity are probed by low-field Landau quantization. A seven-layer hBN/twisted-trilayer-graphene/hBN/graphite/hBN heterostructure assembled by the mica membrane method, with the three graphene layers intentionally misaligned by high angles of about 20°, is fabricated into a Hall bar on SiO2/Si. Low-temperature non-local bend-resistance is measured as a function of total carrier density n and perpendicular magnetic field B, with an applied displacement field condition D = -0.5 V/nm for the non-local map. A double-gate resistance map is also measured at fixed B = 50 mT while sweeping carrier density over approximately -0.2 × 10^12 to +0.2 × 10^12 cm^-2 and displacement field over approximately -0.2 to +0.2 V/nm. The measurement targets ballistic bend resistance and the onset and multiplicity of Landau quantization from the top, middle, and bottom graphene layers.

zero_field_negative_bend_resistance_obse.description: Whether the high-angle twisted trilayer graphene Hall bar exhibited negative bend resistance at zero magnetic field.

landau_quantization_onset_mT.description: The magnetic-field scale at which Landau quantization became detectable in the high-angle twisted trilayer graphene Hall bar.

minimum_distinct_landau_levels_at_50mT.description: The reported lower bound on the number of distinct Landau levels observed in the double-gate map at 50 mT.

experiment_description: Central concept: evaluate whether a heterostructure assembled on a mica cantilever and released by flipping and breaking off the cantilever can function as a high-quality gated graphene Hall-bar device with mica retained as part of the substrate stack. An hBN-encapsulated single-layer graphene heterostructure on a bottom graphite gate is assembled on a freestanding mica cantilever, then flipped and mechanically broken off so the mica remains below the stack. The device is patterned into a Hall bar; the bottom graphite is used as a bottom gate and Ti/Au is used as a top gate, with metal contacts routed over the several-hundred-nanometer-thick mica support. Longitudinal resistivity is measured versus gate voltage during ascending and descending gate sweeps at T = 300 K and again after cooling to T = 1.5 K. Mean free path is extracted at T = 1.5 K as a function of carrier density and compared with the Hall-bar width indicated by the device geometry. The measurement targets hysteresis, Dirac-peak asymmetry, and whether the electronic mean free path reaches the geometric limit.

room_temperature_gate_hysteresis_observe.description: Whether the mica-supported hBN-encapsulated graphene Hall bar exhibited gate-sweep hysteresis at room temperature.

large_dirac_peak_asymmetry_observed.description: Whether the mica-supported graphene Hall bar exhibited a large asymmetry of the Dirac peak between opposite gate-sweep directions.

mean_free_path_limited_by_hall_bar_width.description: Whether the extracted low-temperature electron mean free path was limited by the Hall-bar width.

experiment_description: Central concept: use solvent-free mica-assisted transfer to fabricate suspended 2D heterostructure membranes suitable for nanomechanics, avoiding liquid processing that can damage suspended devices. A single-layer graphene/hBN heterostructure is assembled with the same mica-assisted transfer conditions used for supported stacks and suspended over a circular hole etched in a bottom hBN flake on SiO2, forming a membrane with diameter d = 3 µm. The membrane surface is inspected by peak-force microscopy over the suspended region to target surface continuity and cleanliness. Static force-deflection AFM is then performed at the center of the suspended membrane; force is swept up to approximately 800 nN while indentation is recorded up to approximately 50 nm. The force-deflection curve is fit to the standard continuum-mechanics model for a circular membrane, extracting Young's modulus E and pre-tension N0, where E is the in-plane elastic modulus of the suspended heterostructure membrane and N0 is the built-in membrane tension per unit length.

suspended_slg_hbn_membrane_formed.description: Whether the mica-assisted procedure produced a suspended single-layer graphene/hBN heterostructure membrane over the etched hBN cavity.

youngs_modulus_GPa.description: The Young's modulus extracted from continuum-mechanics fitting of the static AFM force-deflection curve of the suspended SLG/hBN membrane.

pre_tension_N_m.description: The membrane pre-tension per unit length extracted from continuum-mechanics fitting of the static AFM force-deflection curve of the suspended SLG/hBN membrane.

experiment_description: Central concept: characterize the dynamic nanomechanical response of a solvent-free mica-transferred suspended single-layer graphene/hBN heterostructure membrane. The same circular d = 3 µm SLG/hBN membrane suspended over an hBN cavity is mounted inside an Attocube attoDRY800 optical cryostat on an xy positioning stage and cooled to T = 4 K under high vacuum. A power-modulated blue diode laser with wavelength 450 nm actuates membrane motion, and a HeNe red laser with wavelength 633 nm reads out displacement interferometrically; both laser spots are about 1 µm and incident laser powers are below 1 µW. The response amplitude is processed by a vector network analyzer while sweeping drive frequency over the fundamental-mode resonance region around 23.4–24.2 MHz. The resonance spectrum is fit to a linear damped harmonic-oscillator model to extract the resonance frequency f0 and mechanical quality factor Q.

fundamental_resonance_frequency_MHz.description: The fundamental mechanical resonance frequency extracted from the damped harmonic-oscillator fit of the suspended SLG/hBN membrane response.

mechanical_quality_factor.description: The mechanical quality factor extracted from the damped harmonic-oscillator fit of the suspended SLG/hBN membrane response.

experiment_description: Central concept: extend mica-assisted solvent-free transfer to suspended moiré membranes, where substrate-free aligned graphene/hBN superlattices can be examined by scanning probe methods. An aligned single-layer graphene/hBN heterostructure, with the hBN component being 1–2 layers, is fabricated by mica-assisted transfer and suspended over a pre-etched circular cavity in hBN with diameter d = 0.5 µm. Peak-force microscopy adhesion mapping is performed over the full suspended membrane area with nanoscale lateral resolution to target the periodic adhesion modulation of the SLG/hBN moiré lattice across the free-standing region, including assessment of whether the periodic pattern extends to the membrane boundary rather than being limited to a supported substrate region.

suspended_slg_hbn_moire_membrane_formed.description: Whether the mica-assisted transfer produced a suspended aligned SLG/hBN moiré heterostructure membrane over the hBN cavity.

moire_pattern_spans_suspended_membrane.description: Whether the PFM adhesion map detected the SLG/hBN moiré pattern over the suspended membrane surface.

experiment_description: Central concept: test whether mica cantilevers can manipulate non-graphene van der Waals ferroelectrics without polymer residues, using folded 3R-MoS2 as a target structure relevant for mirror-twin-boundary ferroelectric interfaces. A large 3R-MoS2 flake is contacted by a mica cantilever; part of the flake is picked up, folded onto itself, and then delaminated and released by sliding the flake off the cantilever while moving parallel to the substrate surface. The resulting folded and unfolded 3R-MoS2 regions are characterized by AFM over interior areas of each region, away from the fold edge and macroscopic flake boundaries. The measurement targets the topographic roughness of the polymer-free folded interface and the adjacent original region.

folded_3r_mos2_structure_formed.description: Whether the mica-cantilever folding and sliding release procedure produced a folded 3R-MoS2 structure.

folded_region_peak_to_peak_roughness_pm.description: The peak-to-peak topographic roughness of the folded 3R-MoS2 region measured by AFM.

unfolded_region_peak_to_peak_roughness_p.description: The peak-to-peak topographic roughness of the adjacent unfolded 3R-MoS2 region measured by AFM.

experiment_description: Central concept: demonstrate that mica-assisted polymer-free transfer can produce open, uncapped monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenide heterostructures with clean surfaces suitable for optical measurements. A monolayer MoS2 flake is transferred onto an hBN substrate using the mica-assisted procedure; for materials other than hBN, the mica may be mildly treated by UV/O3 at 60 °C for 12 min to improve adhesion. The uncapped MoS2/hBN stack is characterized in ambient air at room temperature. AFM height mapping is used to assess the top surface over the monolayer flake region, and photoluminescence spectroscopy is collected over the visible spectral window corresponding to wavelengths 550–750 nm, targeting the MoS2 excitonic emission from the transferred monolayer.

mos2_surface_rms_roughness_pm.description: The root-mean-square surface roughness of the uncapped monolayer MoS2 on hBN measured by AFM.

room_temperature_pl_peak_energy_eV.description: The photoluminescence peak energy of the uncapped monolayer MoS2 on hBN measured in air at room temperature.

room_temperature_pl_fwhm_meV.description: The full width at half maximum of the room-temperature photoluminescence peak of the uncapped monolayer MoS2 on hBN.

experiment_description: Central concept: assess the broader material compatibility of the mica-assisted polymer-free transfer method beyond graphene and hBN, including exposed conductive layers and air-sensitive magnetic crystals. The same mica-assisted pick-up, stacking, and release strategy is applied to fabricate open single-layer graphene on hBN, hBN-encapsulated few-layer CrBr3, and few-layer FePS3 on hBN. Transfers are performed under dry or inert conditions compatible with mica adhesion control; for top materials with weaker adhesion than hBN, mild UV/O3 treatment of mica at 60 °C for 12 min may be used. Optical microscopy is used over tens-of-micrometers flake-scale areas to assess whether the intended target flakes remain continuous and positioned on the hBN supports or encapsulated between hBN layers, with special attention to the uncapped or air-sensitive active material regions.

uncapped_slg_on_hbn_formed.description: Whether the mica-assisted method produced an uncapped single-layer graphene on hBN heterostructure.

hbn_encapsulated_few_layer_crbr3_formed.description: Whether the mica-assisted method produced an hBN-encapsulated few-layer CrBr3 heterostructure.

few_layer_feps3_on_hbn_formed.description: Whether the mica-assisted method produced a few-layer FePS3 on hBN heterostructure.

experiment_description: Central concept: characterize environmental control of mica adhesion, which underlies the temperature-tunable polymer-free transfer mechanism. Adhesion forces between gold-plated mica cantilevers and representative surfaces including graphite, hBN, and SiO2 are measured by AFM force-deflection methods in ambient conditions while varying humidity and substrate temperature. High-humidity conditions are defined as relative humidity above about 60%, and low-humidity transfer-relevant conditions are compared while increasing the substrate temperature above room temperature up to the range in which the transfer protocol operates. The measurement targets the contact adhesion force between mica and the 2D-material or substrate surfaces, particularly the sensitivity of mica-hBN adhesion to adsorbed water and the reduction of adhesion at elevated temperature.

mica_hbn_adhesion_high_humidity_increase.description: The approximate multiplicative increase in mica-hBN adhesion force under high-humidity conditions relative to lower-humidity conditions.

adhesion_plateau_temperature_lower_bound.description: The lower bound of the substrate-temperature range where the reduced adhesion force reaches a plateau under low-humidity conditions.

adhesion_plateau_temperature_upper_bound.description: The upper bound of the substrate-temperature range where the reduced adhesion force reaches a plateau under low-humidity conditions.
